problem: If the distance between the points $(3a-4,a+2)$ and $(-2,6)$ is minimized, then $a=$
worked_solution:
First, let's compute the *squared* distance $S(a)$ between the two points. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}S(a) & ={(3a-4-(-2))}^{2}+{(a+2-6)}^{2} \\  & =(3a-2)^{2}+(a-4)^{2} \\  & =9{a}^{2}-12a+4+{a}^{2}-8a+16 \\  & =10{a}^{2}-20a+20.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want to minimize $S,$ we compute the derivative ${S}^{′}(a).$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(a) & =20a-20.\end{aligned}
$$

The stationary points of $S(a)$ are the points where the derivative ${S}^{′}(a)=0.$ Solving this equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(a) & =0 \\ 20a-20 & =0 \\ a & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

We can see that ${S}^{″}(1)=20>0.$ Therefore, the squared distance (and therefore the actual distance) reaches a minimum when $b=1.$
